details:
Q1: Which area of the repository should this issue change?
Choices:
A) Clarify phase (`ai-clarify` workflow, `prompts/mode-clarify.txt`)
B) Plan or implement phases (plan/implement workflows and their prompts)
C) Review/autofix pipeline (`review_autofix.yml` and its `scripts/review_autofix_step_*.sh` helpers)
D) Orchestrator (orchestrate_poll, tracking issues, integration-sync)
E) Docs only (README / `docs/`) (RECOMMENDED: lowest risk if no specific defect is in mind)
F) Other: name the exact file(s) or workflow
Q2: What does "better" mean for the area chosen in Q1?
Choices:
A) Fix a specific bug or failure: give the run URL/ID, the error text, or the steps to reproduce it (RECOMMENDED)
B) Reduce cost or latency (token usage, number of GitHub API calls, run time)
C) Improve reliability or recovery (retries, self-heal, fewer stalls)
D) Improve clarity or docs only, with no behavior change
E) Add a new capability: describe it in one or two sentences
Q3: How will we know the change is done?
Choices:
A) A named failing run or test passes afterwards, plus a contract test pinning the fix (RECOMMENDED)
B) A measurable metric improves (state the metric and the target)
C) A reviewer approves the doc or wording change; no metric is needed
Q4: How large a change is acceptable?
Choices:
A) Surgical: the minimum change in the files from Q1, with paired tests and a changelog.d entry (RECOMMENDED)
B) A moderate refactor inside one subsystem, with existing behavior and identifiers preserved
C) Broad cross-workflow changes (**Note:** this conflicts with Q2:D, docs only; choosing both will bring the issue back for re-clarification)
